contract.reader: An engineering student or engineer who knows Boolean logic, latches, timers and state machines (entry 1) and has not programmed a PLC
contract.problem: How control logic runs on industrial hardware: when it sees inputs and changes outputs, how field signals reach it, and how it is programmed in the standard languages
contract.outcome: Compute best- and worst-case response time; explain why a waiting loop freezes a PLC; scale a 4-20 mA input and classify it by NE 43 levels; distinguish functions, function blocks and programs; read one task in LD, FBD, ST and IL; name the rules that make a program safe to run
contract.contribution: One path from hardware and the scan cycle to the IEC 61131-3 languages using entry 1's examples, with timing and scaling claims checked by runnable Python and the 2025 edition change stated
contract.evidence: Two Python programs with real output; worked exercises; IEC 61131-2:2017, IEC 61131-3:2013, IEC 61508, NAMUR NE 43 (2021), Bolton (2015), John and Tiegelkamp (2010), Petruzella (2016)
contract.limitations: Vendor-specific details labeled, not resolved; safety functions out of scope; follows the third edition of IEC 61131-3

findings.location: Section 5 introduction and Section 5.5 SFC (desktop-light-19/20, mobile-light-35/36)
findings.problem: The introduction says the same task shows each language, but SFC has no chart, only a definition, a qualifier table and a link to entry 1
findings.whyItMatters: Readers cannot see steps, transitions or qualifiers, which the section describes in words; the promise is not kept for one of five languages
findings.action: Add a small SFC chart of the mixing tank (four steps, four transitions, N actions), or reword the Section 5 introduction
findings.acceptance: Section 5.5 shows an SFC chart of the mixing tank, or the introduction no longer claims every language is shown on the task

findings.problem: IEC 62061 and ISO 13849-1 are named as the governing safety standards but are missing from the reference list
findings.whyItMatters: On a page classed high risk for safety-relevant guidance, the safety standards the reader is sent to should be easy to find
findings.action: Add IEC 62061 and ISO 13849-1 to the references in house style
findings.acceptance: Both standards appear in the live reference list

findings.location: Section 2.2 response-time bound (mobile-light-09); Section 3.4 scaling equations (mobile-light-20)
findings.problem: At 360 px the upper bound is cut and the second scaling equation (counts-to-units, x = x_lo + ...) is entirely off-screen, no scroll cue
findings.whyItMatters: The scaling formula is the result of Section 3.4; recoverable from the worked numbers, so minor
findings.action: Put the two scaling equations on separate lines and break the response-time bound after the middle term
findings.acceptance: At 360 px both scaling equations and both bounds are fully visible

findings.location: Section 2.1 scan-cycle flowchart; Section 5.2 FBD diagram
findings.problem: Neither diagram has a caption or accessible title (facts.json: 2 SVG figures without title)
findings.whyItMatters: Standards 6.8 asks captions to say what to notice; screen-reader users get nothing
findings.action: Add accTitle/accDescr and a one-sentence caption to each diagram
findings.acceptance: Both diagrams have visible captions and facts.json reports 0 SVG figures without title
